rationale: The dominant leg, lct/at, is a plain short-term leverage ratio (a long-known distress/leverage proxy), while the second leg implies that *more* long-term debt issuance predicts *higher* returns — directly contrary to the well-documented debt-issuance/external-financing anomaly — and dltis's large mass of zero/missing values makes that rank leg mostly ties, so the wedge is unlikely to identify the maturity-mismatch mechanism claimed.

Since dvt/at is zero for most firms and heavily tied, the signal is essentially NEG(oancf/at), i.e. a rediscovery of the cash-flow-to-assets/profitability premium, while the dividend leg pushes against the expected sign (high payout is itself a known positive predictor), so any result will be uninterpretable as a "payout sustainability" test.

target_name: Own-history divergence of external and internal funding
rationale: The within-firm timing dimension is genuinely untested in the archive and the demeaning of firm-level levels is a coherent response to the prior product-form failures, though both legs still point in the same direction as known issuance and cash-flow effects, and a 5-period annual TS_RANK is coarse enough that the "regime switch" tails may be noisy.

The positive-sign, outflow-side conditional is a legitimate contrast to the rest of the archive, but the repurchase leg alone is the well-known buyback/net-payout-yield anomaly and prstkc is zero for most firms, so the realistic risk is that the signal simply reprices repurchasers with a low-working-capital tilt rather than isolating the costly-signalling mechanism.

txt/at is far more a profitability proxy than a tax-status proxy (low taxes paid mostly means low pre-tax income), so the expression reduces to "debt issuance minus profitability" — a sum of two established anomalies with the same sign — and provides no identification of the tax-shield channel the hypothesis rests on.

(oancf − ib)/at is the negative of total accruals, so subtracting its rank makes this literally "net share issuance rank plus accruals rank" — a mechanical stack of two of the most heavily published anomalies pointing the same way — which contradicts the stated aim of separating rather than combining them.
